Published online:

Geographic focus:
Bangladesh (South Asia)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — documents existing power crisis and prior capacity figures
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ongoing fuel supply disruptions, Middle East tensions affecting near-term LNG/oil procurement
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — renewable targets for 2027/2030/2040, multi-year structural energy transition

Synopsis:
Bangladesh is rolling out a feed-in tariff incentive (10.50 taka/kWh for 3 years) for rooftop solar + battery systems installed before Feb 2027, responding to a severe power crisis peaking at ~4,000 MW of shortfall in August 2026. The crisis is driven by natural gas scarcity, coal/fuel oil constraints, and heightened supply risk from Middle East instability (Iran war context). The programme targets 20% renewables by 2030 (5,500 MW) and 30% by 2040. Rooftop solar is prioritized as a fast, land-efficient deployment path for a densely populated country heavily exposed to imported fossil fuel price volatility.
